verses.21:1: Then the heads of the fathers' houses of the sons of Levi came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the tribal heads of the fathers' houses from the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:2: And they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to dwell in, and the pasturelands for our livestock."
verses.21:3: So the sons of Israel gave to the Levites, in taking their inheritance by the command of the Lord, the cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:4: And the lot came out for the clan of Kohath; and to the sons of Aaron the priests, the Levites, there fell by lot from the tribe of Judah, from the tribe of Simeon, and from the tribe of Benjamin thirteen cities.
verses.21:5: And to the remaining sons of Kohath there fell by lot out of the tribe of Ephraim, out of the tribe of Dan, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh ten cities.
verses.21:6: And to the sons of Gershon from the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan came thirteen cities.
verses.21:7: And among the sons of Merari according to their clans, from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun, there fell by lot twelve cities.
verses.21:8: So the sons of Israel gave to the Levites the cities and their pasturelands by lot, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.21:9: And the tribe of the sons of Judah, the tribe of the sons of Simeon, and those from the tribe of the sons of Benjamin gave these cities, and they were assigned by name
verses.21:10: to the sons of Aaron, from the clan of Kohath of the sons of Levi, for this became the lot.
verses.21:11: And he gave them Kiriath-arba, the mother city of the Anakim (which is Hebron), in the hill country of Judah; but the pasturelands around it
verses.21:12: and the fields of the city and its villages Joshua gave to the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh for a possession.
verses.21:13: And to the sons of Aaron he gave the city of refuge for the manslayer, Hebron and the lands set apart with it, and Libnah and the lands set apart adjoining it,
verses.21:14: and Ailom and the lands set apart for it, and Tema and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:15: and Gella and the lands set apart for it, and Debir and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:16: and Asa and the lands set apart for it, and Tany and the lands set apart for it, and Beth-shemesh and the lands set apart for it: nine cities from these two tribes.
verses.21:17: And from the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon and the lands set apart for it, and Gatheth and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:18: and Anathoth and the lands set apart for it, and Gamala and the lands set apart for it: four cities.
verses.21:19: All the cities of the sons of Aaron the priests were thirteen.
verses.21:20: And to the clans of the sons of Kohath, the Levites who remained from the sons of Kohath, there came the city of their priests from the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.21:21: And they gave them the city of refuge for the manslayer, Shechem and the lands set apart for it, and Gezer with its adjoining places and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:22: and Beth-horon and the lands set apart for it: four cities.
verses.21:23: And out of the tribe of Dan, Elkothaim and the lands set apart for it, and Gethedan and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:24: and Aijalon and the lands set apart for it, and Gath-rimmon and the lands set apart for it: four cities.
verses.21:25: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach and the lands set apart for it, and Jebatha and the lands set apart for it: two cities.
verses.21:26: All the cities were ten, with the set-apart lands adjoining them, for the clans of the remaining sons of Kohath.
verses.21:27: And to the sons of Gershon, the Levites, they gave out of the half-tribe of Manasseh the cities set apart for the manslayers—Golan in Bashan and the lands set apart for it, and Bosora and the lands set apart for it: two cities.
verses.21:28: And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion and the lands set apart for it, and Debba and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:29: and Remmath and the lands set apart for it, and Fountain of Letters and the lands set apart for it: four cities.
verses.21:30: And out of the tribe of Asher, Basellan and the lands set apart for it, and Dabbon and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:31: and Helkath and the lands set apart for it, and Rehob and the lands set apart for it: four cities.
verses.21:32: And out of the tribe of Naphtali, the city set apart for the manslayer, Kedesh in Galilee and the lands set apart for it, and Nemmath and the lands set apart for it, and Themmon and the lands set apart for it: three cities.
verses.21:33: All the cities of Gershon according to their clans were thirteen cities.
verses.21:34: And to the clan of the sons of Merari, the remaining Levites, they gave out of the tribe of Zebulun Maan and its pasturelands, and Kedesh and its pasturelands,
verses.21:35: and Sella and its pasturelands: three cities.
verses.21:36: And beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, out of the tribe of Reuben, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Bezer in the wilderness, Miso, and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands,
verses.21:37: and Dekmon and its pasturelands, and Mapha and its pasturelands: four cities.
verses.21:38: And from the tribe of Gad, the city of refuge for the manslayer, even Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, Kamein and its pasturelands,
verses.21:39: and Heshbon and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands: all of them four cities.
verses.21:40: All the cities for the sons of Merari according to their clans, who remained from the tribe of Levi—their borders were twelve cities.
verses.21:41: All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel were forty-eight cities, and their pasturelands
verses.21:42: around these cities—a city and the pasturelands around the city for all these cities. And Joshua finished dividing the land within their borders. And the sons of Israel gave a portion to Joshua according to the command of the Lord; they gave him the city for which he asked—Timnath-serah they gave him in the hill country of Ephraim. And Joshua built the city and dwelt in it. And Joshua took the stone knives with which he had circumcised the sons of Israel who were born on the way in the wilderness, and he placed them in Timnath-serah.
verses.21:43: And the Lord gave to Israel all the land that He swore to give to their fathers, and they received it as an inheritance and dwelt in it.
verses.21:44: And the Lord granted them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers; not one stood before them out of all their enemies; the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands.
verses.21:45: Not one failed of all the good words that the Lord had spoken to the sons of Israel; every one came to pass.
verses.22:1: Then Joshua summoned the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh,
verses.22:2: and said to them, "You have listened to all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and you have heeded my voice according to all that he commanded you.
verses.22:3: You have not forsaken your brethren these many days; until this present day you have kept the commandment of the Lord your God.
verses.22:4: And now the Lord our God has given rest to our brethren, just as He spoke to them. Now therefore, turn back and depart to your houses and to the land of your possession, which Moses gave to you beyond the Jordan.
verses.22:5: Yet take diligent heed to do the commandments and the law which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded us to do: to love the Lord our God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments and to cling to Him, and to serve Him with all your mind and with all your soul."
verses.22:6: So Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their houses.
verses.22:7: Now to half the tribe of Manasseh Moses gave an inheritance in the region of Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave one among their brethren beyond the Jordan by the sea. And when Joshua sent them away to their houses and blessed them,
verses.22:8: they departed to their houses with much wealth, and very many livestock, and silver, and gold, and iron, and abundant clothing; and they divided the spoil of the enemies with their brethren.
verses.22:9: So the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of the sons of Manasseh journeyed from the sons of Israel at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go away to Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they had inherited by the command of the Lord through the hand of Moses.
verses.22:10: And they came to Gilgal of the Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan; and the sons of Gad, and the sons of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to behold.
verses.22:11: And the sons of Israel heard it said, "Behold, the sons of Gad, and the sons of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the borders of the land of Canaan, at Gilead of the Jordan, across from the sons of Israel."
verses.22:12: Then all the sons of Israel gathered together at Shiloh, to go up and wage war against them.
verses.22:13: And the sons of Israel sent to the sons of Reuben, and to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of half the tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the high priest,
verses.22:14: and ten of the rulers with him, one ruler from each father's house out of all the tribes of Israel; they were rulers of fathers' houses, commanders of thousands of Israel.
verses.22:15: And they came to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of Reuben, and to those of half the tribe of Manasseh, into Gilead, and they spoke to them, saying,
verses.22:16: "Thus says the whole congregation of the Lord: What is this trespass that you have committed before the God of Israel, turning away today from the Lord by building for yourselves an altar, that you should become rebels against the Lord?
verses.22:17: Is the sin of Peor a small thing to us? For we have not been cleansed from it until this day, and a plague came in the congregation of the Lord.
verses.22:18: And you have turned away today from the Lord! And it shall come to pass, if you rebel today against the Lord, that tomorrow wrath shall be upon all Israel.
verses.22:19: And now, if the land of your possession is too small, cross over into the land of the possession of the Lord, where the tabernacle of the Lord dwells, and take an inheritance among us; and do not become rebels against God, and do not rebel against the Lord by building an altar apart from the altar of the Lord our God.
verses.22:20: Behold, did not Achar the son of Zerah surely trespass concerning the accursed thing, and wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel? And that one man alone died in his own sin."
verses.22:21: Then the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the commanders of thousands of Israel, saying,
verses.22:22: "God is God—the Lord! And God, even God, Himself knows, and Israel itself shall know: if in rebellion we have trespassed before the Lord, may He not deliver us on this day;
verses.22:23: and if we have built for ourselves an altar to depart from the Lord our God, to offer upon it a sacrifice of burnt offerings, or to offer upon it a sacrifice of peace offerings, the Lord shall require it.
verses.22:24: Rather, out of anxious concern for a matter we have done this, saying, Lest tomorrow your children say to our children, 'What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
verses.22:25: And the Lord has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, and you have no portion in the Lord.' And your sons would estrange our sons, so that they would not revere the Lord.
verses.22:26: And we resolved to do thus, to build this altar—not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifices,
verses.22:27: but that this may be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of the Lord before Him with our burnt offerings, and with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings; and your children shall not say to our children tomorrow, 'You have no portion in the Lord.'
verses.22:28: And we said that if it should ever come to pass that they speak to us and to our generations tomorrow, then they shall say, 'Behold the likeness of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between you and between us and between our sons.'
verses.22:29: Far be it from us, therefore, to turn away from the Lord in these present days, to rebel against the Lord so that we should build an altar for burnt offerings, and for the salamin sacrifices, and for the peace offering, besides the altar of the Lord which is before His tabernacle."
verses.22:30: Now when Phinehas the priest and all the rulers of the congregation of Israel who were with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh spoke, it pleased them.
verses.22:31: And Phinehas the priest said to the sons of Reuben, and to the sons of Gad, and to half the tribe of Manasseh, "Today we know that the Lord is with us, because you have not committed a trespass before the Lord, and because you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord."
verses.22:32: Then Phinehas the priest and the rulers returned from the sons of Reuben, and from the sons of Gad, and from half the tribe of Manasseh, out of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and reported the words to them.
verses.22:33: And it pleased the sons of Israel; and they spoke to the sons of Israel, and blessed the God of the sons of Israel, and said no longer to go up against them to war, to destroy the land of the sons of Reuben, and of the sons of Gad, and of half the tribe of Manasseh; and they dwelt upon it.
verses.22:34: And Joshua named the altar of those of Reuben, and of those of Gad, and of half the tribe of Manasseh, and said, "It is a witness between them that the Lord is their God."
verses.23:1: Now it came to pass after many days, after the Lord had given rest to Israel from all their enemies round about, that Joshua was old and advanced in days.
verses.23:2: And Joshua summoned all the sons of Israel, and their council of elders, and their rulers, and their scribes, and their judges, and said to them, "I have grown old and am advanced in days.
verses.23:3: And you have seen all that the Lord our God has done to all these nations before our face, for it is the Lord our God who has fought for us.
verses.23:4: Behold, just as I spoke to you, these nations that remain to you are in the lots for your tribes, from the Jordan—even all the nations that I have destroyed—and from the Great Sea it shall mark the border toward the setting of the sun.
verses.23:5: And the Lord our God, He shall destroy them from before our face until they perish; and He shall send the wild beasts against them until He destroys them and their kings from before your face; and inherit their land, just as the Lord our God spoke to you.
verses.23:6: Be exceedingly strong, therefore, to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that you may not turn aside to the right hand or to the left;
verses.23:7: so that you do not enter in among these nations that remain, and the names of their gods shall not be named among you; you shall by no means bow down to them, nor shall you serve them,
verses.23:8: but to the Lord our God you shall cling, just as you have done until this day.
verses.23:9: And the Lord shall destroy them from before your face—nations great and strong—and no one has withstood before us until this day.
verses.23:10: One of you pursued a thousand, for the Lord our God fought for us, just as He spoke to us.
verses.23:11: And take diligent heed to love the Lord our God.
verses.23:12: For if you turn back and join yourselves to these remaining nations that are with you, and make marriages with them, and mingle yourselves with them and they with you,
verses.23:13: know for certain that the Lord shall no longer continue to destroy these nations from before your face; rather, they shall be to you as snares and stumbling blocks, and as nails in your heels and darts in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which the Lord your God has given you.
verses.23:14: And I am departing the way, even as all who are upon the earth; and you shall know in your heart and in your soul that not one word has fallen from all the words which the Lord our God spoke concerning all things pertaining to us; not one of them has failed.
verses.23:15: And it shall come to pass that just as all the good words which the Lord spoke to us have come upon us, so shall the Lord God bring upon you all the evil words, until He destroys you from this good land which the Lord has given you,
verses.23:16: when you transgress the covenant of the Lord our God, which He commanded us, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them."
verses.24:1: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shiloh, and called together their elders and their scribes and their judges, and he set them before God.
verses.24:2: And Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: 'Beyond the river your fathers dwelt from the beginning, Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor; and they served other gods.
verses.24:3: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the river, and led him throughout all the land; and I multiplied his seed and gave him Isaac,
verses.24:4: and to Isaac, Jacob and Esau; I gave to Esau Mount Seir to inherit for himself. And Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt, and they became there a great, populous, and mighty nation; and the Egyptians afflicted them.'
verses.24:5: And they struck Egypt with the things that they did to them. And after these things He brought out
verses.24:6: our fathers out of Egypt, and you entered into the Red Sea; and the Egyptians pursued after our fathers with chariots and with horses into the Red Sea.
verses.24:7: And we cried out to the Lord, and He placed a cloud and thick darkness between us and the Egyptians; and He brought the sea upon them and covered them. And your eyes saw all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt; and you were in the wilderness many days.
verses.24:8: And He brought us into the land of the Amorites who dwelt beyond the Jordan, and the Lord delivered them into our hands; and you inherited their land, and utterly destroyed them from before your face.
verses.24:9: And Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and arrayed himself in battle against Israel; and he sent and summoned Balaam to curse us.
verses.24:10: And the Lord your God would not destroy you; indeed, with a blessing He blessed us, and He delivered us out of their hands, and gave them over.
verses.24:11: And you crossed over the Jordan and came to Jericho; and those who dwelt in Jericho fought against us: the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite and the Hittite and the Girgashite; and the Lord delivered them into our hands.
verses.24:12: And He sent out the hornet before us, and drove them out from before our face—twelve kings of the Amorites—not with your sword nor with your bow.
verses.24:13: And He gave you a land for which you did not labor, and cities which you did not build, and you were settled in them; and of vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant, you shall eat.
verses.24:14: And now fear the Lord and serve Him in uprightness and in righteousness; and put away the foreign gods which our fathers served beyond the river and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.
verses.24:15: But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve: whether the gods of your fathers who were beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorites, among whom you dwell in their land; but I and my household will serve the Lord, for He is holy."
verses.24:16: And the people answered and said, "Far be it from us to forsake the Lord so as to serve other gods.
verses.24:17: The Lord our God, He is God; He brought us and our fathers up out of Egypt, and guarded us throughout all the way in which we journeyed, and among all the nations through whom we passed;
verses.24:18: and the Lord cast out the Amorite and all the nations dwelling in the land from before our face. Indeed, we also will serve the Lord, for He is our God."
verses.24:19: And Joshua said to the people, "You will by no means be able to serve the Lord, for He is a holy God; and being jealous, He will not pardon your sins and your iniquities.
verses.24:20: Whenever you forsake the Lord and serve other gods, He will come upon you and afflict you and utterly consume you, in return for the good He has done for you."
verses.24:21: And the people said to Joshua, "No, but we will serve the Lord."
verses.24:22: And Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord, to serve Him.
verses.24:23: And now put away the foreign gods that are among you, and direct your heart to the Lord God of Israel."
verses.24:24: And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the Lord, and we will obey His voice."
verses.24:25: And Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day, and gave them a law and a judgment in Shiloh, before the tabernacle of the God of Israel.
verses.24:26: And he wrote these words in a book, the law of God; and Joshua took a great stone and set it up under the terebinth tree before the Lord.
verses.24:27: And Joshua said to the people, "Behold, this stone shall be among you for a witness, for it has heard all the things spoken to it by the Lord, whatever He has spoken to us today; and this stone shall be among you for a witness in the last days, whenever you deal falsely with the Lord my God."
verses.24:28: And Joshua sent the people away, and they departed, each one to his own place.
verses.24:29: And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who prolonged their days after Joshua and who had seen all the works of the Lord which He had done for Israel.
verses.24:30: And it came to pass after these things that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being one hundred and ten years old.
verses.24:31: And they buried him by the borders of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead; there they placed with him in the tomb in which they buried him the stone knives with which he had circumcised the sons of Israel at Gilgal, when He brought them out of Egypt, just as the Lord commanded them; and they are there to this very day.
verses.24:32: And the sons of Israel brought up the bones of Joseph out of Egypt and buried them in Shechem, in the portion of the field which Jacob had acquired from the Amorites who dwelt in Shechem for one hundred ewe lambs.
verses.24:33: And it came to pass after these things that Eleazar the son of Aaron, the high priest, died and was buried in Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which he had given him in the hill country of Ephraim. On that day the sons of Israel took the ark of God and carried it about among themselves; and Phinehas served as priest in the place of Eleazar his father until he died, and he was buried in their own Gibeah. And the sons of Israel departed, each one to his own place and to his own city. And the sons of Israel worshiped Astarte and Ashtaroth and the gods of the nations around them; and the Lord delivered them into the hands of Eglon the king of Moab, and he ruled over them eighteen years.

notes.1:1: Greek Naue corresponds to Hebrew Nun, the father of Joshua.
notes.1:4: The Greek reads Antilebanon, the mountain range east of Lebanon, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Lebanon, and omits the phrase concerning the land of the Hittites.
notes.1:8: The Greek verb is third-person singular ("it shall prosper your ways," referring to the book of the law), whereas the Hebrew has second-person singular ("you shall make your ways prosperous").
notes.2:14: In the Greek text, Rahab speaks the second half of this verse ("When the Lord delivers the city to you..."), whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text the two men continue speaking.
notes.2:18: The Greek reads "into a part of the city," whereas the Hebrew reads "into the land."
notes.2:19: The Greek legal terms "guilty for himself" and "we shall be guilty" correspond to the Hebrew blood-guilt expressions concerning blood being on one's head.
notes.3:4: "Since yesterday and the third day before" is a literal Greek rendering of a Hebrew idiom meaning "heretofore" or "previously."
notes.3:8: The Greek specifies entering "into the midst of the water of the Jordan," whereas the Hebrew reads "to the edge of the water of the Jordan."
notes.3:16: Greek Kathiairein is a distinct place name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan"; the Greek also concludes with the people standing opposite Jericho rather than crossing over.
notes.4:4: Greek reads "twelve distinguished men" (ton endoxon), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "twelve men whom he had appointed."
notes.4:11: Greek reads "and the stones before them" (kai hoi lithoi emprosthen auton), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "and the priests, in the presence of the people."
notes.4:24: Greek reads "the power of the Lord is mighty" and "in every work" (en panti ergo), where the Masoretic Text reads "the hand of the LORD is mighty" and "forever" (lit. "all the days").
notes.5:1: Greek reads "Phoenicia" here (and "the Phoenicians" in 5:12), where the Masoretic Text refers to the Canaanites and Canaan.
notes.5:2: Greek reads "sit down and circumcise" (kathisas periteme), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew root for "sit" where the Masoretic Text has "circumcise again a second time."
notes.5:5: Greek specifies "forty-two years" (versus Masoretic "forty years") and transliterates Hebrew midbar ("wilderness") as the proper name "Madbaritis."
notes.5:14: Unlike the Masoretic Text, the Greek omits both "No" and "and worshiped," having Joshua fall on his face and address the chief commander as "Master" (Despota).
notes.6:3: The Greek text of verses 6:3-5 is much shorter than the Masoretic Text and omits verse 6:4 entirely, moving directly from 6:3 to 6:5.
notes.6:8: Greek continues Joshua's instructions as direct commands in the imperative mood through verses 6:8-9 (and reads "sacred trumpets"), whereas the Masoretic Text shifts to narrative here.
notes.6:15: Greek reads "six times" here, followed by "on the seventh circuit" in 6:16, whereas the Masoretic Text has "seven times" in 6:15.
notes.6:17: Greek reads "the Lord of hosts" (Kyrio sabaoth), whereas the Masoretic Text has simply "the LORD."
notes.6:26: Greek adds a fulfillment notice absent from the Masoretic Text of Joshua (cf. 1 Kings 16:34), naming "Ozan of Bethel" (for Hiel) and "Abiron" (for Abiram), and rendering Segub as "the youngest who survived" (to elachisto diasothenti).
notes.7:1: The Greek text reads "Achar" and "Zambri" (corresponding to "Achan" and "Zabdi" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text); the form "Achar" matches 1 Chronicles 2:7 and directly echoes the place name "Achor" in 7:24-26.
notes.7:7: Following the Greek text, Joshua asks why "Your servant" brought the people across the Jordan, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text addresses God directly ("why have You brought").
notes.7:21: The Greek describes the garment as a "fine embroidered robe" (rather than "Babylonian garment" as in the Hebrew) and measures the silver and gold in "didrachmas," the standard Septuagint equivalent for shekels.
notes.7:24: The Greek text includes both the translated name "the Valley of Achor" and the Hebrew transliteration "Emek-Achor" (also in 7:26) within the same verse.
notes.8:12: The Greek text presents a single ambush of thirty thousand men (8:3) stationed on the west (literally "from the sea," as also in 8:9), omitting the separate five-thousand-man ambush and verse 13 found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:18: The Greek term denotes a heavy javelin or spear; the Greek text also includes the assurance that the ambush will rise up swiftly as part of the Lord's spoken command.
notes.8:25: The Greek text omits verse 26 (concerning Joshua keeping his javelin outstretched) and moves directly to the taking of the spoils in verse 27.
notes.8:29: The Greek phrase literally means "double wood," indicating a forked tree or two-post gallows; the Greek also states that the king's body was cast "into the pit" rather than at the city gate as in the Hebrew, and places the Mount Ebal passage (Hebrew 8:30-35) after 9:2.
notes.9:1: The Greek reads "Anti-Lebanon" rather than "Lebanon" and includes the Girgashites among the listed peoples.
notes.9:2: In the Septuagint, the Mount Ebal altar and reading of the law (Hebrew 8:30-35) stand here; "the repetition of the law" renders Greek to deuteronomion (literally "the second law").
notes.9:4: The Greek reads "upon their shoulders" rather than "upon their donkeys" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.9:7: The Greek reads "the Horite" rather than "the Hivite" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.9:17: The Greek renders these city names as "Beeron" (Hebrew Beeroth) and translates Kiriath-jearim as "the cities of Jarein."
notes.10:1: The Greek names the king of Jerusalem "Adoni-bezek" rather than "Adoni-zedek" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.10:3: The Greek preserves distinct names for the allied kings and one city: Elam (Hebrew Hoham), Pheidon (Piram), Jephthah (Japhia), Dabein (Debir), and Adullam (Eglon; also in 10:5, 23, 34, 37); in 10:5 the Greek calls them "the five kings of the Jebusites" rather than "Amorites."
notes.10:10: The Greek reads "Horonein" (omitting "Beth-" from Hebrew Beth-horon; also in 10:11). In 10:13 the Greek states that God Himself took vengeance and omits the reference to the Book of Jashar, and 10:15 is absent in the Septuagint.
notes.10:21: The Greek reads "not one of the children of Israel muttered with his tongue," whereas the Hebrew reads "no one moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel."
notes.10:33: The Greek reads "Elam king of Gaza" rather than "Horam king of Gezer." In 10:40 the Greek transliterates the Negev and the slopes as "Nabai" and "Asedoth," and 10:43 is absent in the Septuagint.
notes.11:1: The Septuagint reads Jabis, Marron, Symoon, and Azeiph where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Jabin, Madon, Shimron, and Achshaph; similar Septuagint proper-name forms appear throughout chapters 11–12.
notes.11:6: The Greek reads "routed" (tetropomenous) rather than the Hebrew "slain," reflecting a distinct Septuagint textual reading.
notes.11:19: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Septuagint omits the exception clause regarding the Hivites of Gibeon, stating simply that Israel took every city in war.
notes.11:22: The Septuagint names only Gaza and Aseldo (corresponding to Ashdod) as places where the Anakim remained, omitting Gath found in the Hebrew text.
notes.11:23: The Greek reads the plural pronoun "them" (autous), referring collectively to the conquered lands and territories, where the Hebrew has the singular "it."
notes.12:4: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew Rephaim as "the giants" (ton giganton) and introduces a finite verb ("he was left").
notes.12:7: The Septuagint specifies "the kings of the Amorites" where the Hebrew reads "the kings of the land," and names the mountain Chelcha (compare Achel in 11:17 and Halak in the Hebrew).
notes.12:24: The Septuagint lists the kings without the repeated Hebrew word "one" and gives the total as "twenty-nine" rather than "thirty-one"; because of a doublet in 12:14 (Airath and Arath), thirty individual kings are named in this Greek list.
notes.13:3: The Septuagint reads "the uninhabited region" (τῆς ἀοικήτου) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the river "Shihor," and uses "the Hivite" (τῷ Εὐαίῳ) where the Hebrew reads the Avvim.
notes.13:5: "Galiath of the Philistines" and "Galgaa" preserve Septuagint-distinct names where the Hebrew has "the Gebalites" and "Baal-gad"; similarly "Taphek" (13:4), "Masereth-memphonmaim" (13:6), "Daidaban" (13:9), and "Acha" (13:11) reflect the Greek text.
notes.13:8: The opening clause extending the Lord's speech to the Great Sea is a Septuagint addition absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.13:21: The Greek preserves distinctive readings across 13:17–27—including "spoils of Sihon" (ἔναρα Σειών) and "those who dwelt in Sihon" here, "in the rout" (ἐν τῇ ῥοπῇ) in 13:22, and Septuagint place names such as "House of Meelboth," "Serada," "Seion on Mount Enab," "Araba," "Arad," "Enadom," and "Othargaei."
notes.13:28: The clause "they shall turn their neck against their enemies, for it came to be according to their clans" is a distinctive Septuagint addition not present in the Hebrew text.
notes.14:2: The Septuagint reads "by the hand of Joshua" where the Hebrew has "by the hand of Moses," followed by a briefer transition ("from beyond the Jordan") in 14:3.
notes.14:7: "according to his mind" (κατὰ τὸν νοῦν αὐτοῦ) follows the Greek text literally, where the Hebrew reads "as it was in my heart."
notes.14:15: The Septuagint names ancient Hebron "the city of Argob" and calls it "the mother city [μητρόπολις] of the Anakim," where the Hebrew reads "Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim."
notes.15:1: The Greek text reads "Judea" (Ioudaias) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Edom." Throughout this boundary description, Greek lips ("southwest") represents both southern and western directions.
notes.15:7: The Greek reads "the fourth part of the Valley of Achor" and "Taagad" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Debir from the Valley of Achor" and "Gilgal," and translates En-shemesh literally as "Spring of the Sun" (compare "City of the Sun" in 15:10).
notes.15:13: The Greek reads "by the command of God" and calls the city of Arba the "mother city" (metropolin) of Anak, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "father of Anak."
notes.15:19: The Greek treats the Hebrew expressions for "springs of water" and "the upper springs and the lower springs" as proper names: "Boththanis" and "the upper Gonaithla and the lower Gonaithla."
notes.15:21: The Septuagint list of southern cities in verses 21-32 preserves numerous distinct Greek place-name forms (including Kaibaiseleel, Ara, Ikam, Regma, Aruel, Hasorionain, Mainam, Balmainan, Sen, Salmaa, Serei, Cholaseola, Bakok, Elboudad, Macharim, Sethennak, Labos, Sale, and Eromoth) that differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:44: The Greek counts ten cities in this district (including Akiezei, Kezib, Bathesar, and Aijalon) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text counts nine; throughout verses 33-62, the Septuagint preserves numerous distinct Greek city-name forms that differ from the Hebrew.
notes.15:46: The Greek renders the Hebrew phrase for "and to the sea" as the place name "Gemna."
notes.15:59: The Septuagint preserves a major additional district of eleven cities headed by Tekoa and Ephrathah (Bethlehem) that is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:62: The Greek omits the heading "In the wilderness" at verse 61, reads "the cities of Sodom" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "City of Salt," and counts seven cities rather than six.
notes.15:63: The Greek reads "destroy them" (Hebrew "drive them out"), omits "with the sons of Judah," and ends with "until that day" rather than "to this day."
notes.16:2: The Greek reads "to Bethel" (whereas the Hebrew reads "from Bethel to Luz") and preserves the Septuagint-distinct names Chatarothi (Hebrew Archites) and, in verse 3, Haptalim (Hebrew Japhletites).
notes.16:6: Verses 5 through 8 preserve several distinctive Septuagint geographical forms, including Ashtaroth and Erok, Gazara, Hicasmon, Therma, Thenasa and Sellesa, Janoka, Macho, Taphu, and Chelkana.
notes.16:10: The Septuagint adds an account of Pharaoh king of Egypt capturing and burning Gezer and giving it to his daughter as a dowry (paralleling 1 Kings 9:16), in place of the Hebrew statement that the Canaanites became forced laborers.
notes.17:5: The Greek reads "from Anassa, and the plain of Labek," a notable Septuagint divergence from the Hebrew text ("ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan"); verse 2 likewise preserves the Septuagint-distinct clan names Jezi, Kelez, Jeziel, and Symarim.
notes.17:7: The Greek preserves several Septuagint-distinct geographical names across verses 7 through 11, including Delanath, sons of Anath, Hiamin, Jassib, Thaphthoth, Karana, Jariel, Jaseb (for Asher in verse 10), Kaithoan, and "the third part of Mapheta" (verse 11).
notes.17:9: The Greek reads "a terebinth tree," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonantal text that the Masoretic Text reads as "these [cities]."
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "choice horses and iron" (Hebrew "chariots of iron") and "the valley of Israel" (Hebrew "the valley of Jezreel").
notes.18:4: At the end of verse 4 and into verse 5, the Greek shifts briefly into third-person narrative ("And they came to him, and he divided for them seven portions") before resuming Joshua's direct address in verse 6.
notes.18:12: Mabdaritis Bethon transliterates the Hebrew phrase for "the wilderness of Beth-aven"; verses 13 through 17 also preserve distinctive Septuagint forms such as Maatarothorech, Gasin, Galiaoth, Aithamin, and Baion of the sons of Reuben.
notes.18:16: The Greek transliterates "the valley of the son of Hinnom" and "the Valley of Rephaim" as Sonnam, Emekraphain, and Gaienna (Gehenna).
notes.18:22: The city name Sara directly transliterates the Septuagint-distinct Greek place name Σαρά (corresponding to Hebrew Zemaraim, not the patriarch's wife Sarah), alongside the Septuagint forms Bethabara and Besana.
notes.18:28: Verses 21 through 28 preserve numerous distinctive Septuagint city names (such as Bethegaio, Amekasis, Massema, Miron, Hamoke, Phira, Kaphan, Nakan, Selekan, and Gabaothjarim), render Hebrew Kiriath literally as "cities," and total "thirteen cities" (Hebrew "fourteen").
notes.19:6: The Greek text reads 'Batharoth, and their fields' rather than the Hebrew 'Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen,' while retaining the total of thirteen cities.
notes.19:15: The Greek text reads 'Jericho' and 'Bethman' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Idalah' and 'Bethlehem,' and omits the Hebrew summary of twelve cities.
notes.19:26: The Greek text reads 'Seion and Labanath' (Greek Seion, a northern border site distinct from Mount Zion) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Shihor-libnath.'
notes.19:47: Here and in verse 48, the Greek text diverges substantially from the Hebrew, incorporating material parallel to Judges 1:34–35 concerning the Amorites pressing Dan in the hill country.
notes.19:48: The Greek text names 'the sons of Judah' fighting 'Lachish' and renaming it 'Lasenndak,' whereas the Hebrew text attributes this campaign to the sons of Dan against 'Leshem,' renamed 'Dan.'
notes.19:50: The Greek text reads 'of God' and 'Thamarchares' (Timnath-heres), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'of the Lord' and 'Timnath-serah.'
notes.20:3: The Old Greek text moves directly from verse 3 to verse 7, omitting the procedural instructions found in verses 4–6 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text. 'Avenger of blood' renders Greek ho anchisteuon to haima, literally 'the kinsman who claims the blood.'
notes.20:7: The Greek verbs in verses 7–8 are singular ('he set apart,' 'he gave'), making Joshua the subject rather than plural Israel, and verse 7 renders Kiriath-arba as 'the city of Arbok.'
notes.21:11: The Greek reads "mother city of the Anakim" and links "the pasturelands around it" grammatically with v. 12 as part of what Joshua gave to the sons of Caleb, whereas the Hebrew text assigns Hebron's pasturelands to the Levites.
notes.21:20: The Greek text reads "the city of their priests" (polis ton hiereon auton), a distinctive Septuagint textual reading where the Hebrew has "the cities of their lot"; in v. 22 only three Ephraimite cities are named though the total remains four.
notes.21:29: "Fountain of Letters" translates the Greek Pegen grammaton, corresponding to En-gannim in the Hebrew text; several other Levitical town names across vv. 14–38 (such as Ailom, Tema, Gella, Jebatha, Bosora, Maan, Dekmon, and Kamein) likewise preserve distinctive Septuagint forms.
notes.21:36: The Septuagint includes the four Reubenite cities in vv. 36–37, treats the Hebrew term for "tableland" as the proper name Miso, and reads "Jazer" both here and in v. 39 (while vv. 34–35 name three Zebulunite cities though v. 40 sums the Merarite cities as twelve).
notes.21:42: The Septuagint adds an extended conclusion to v. 42 recounting Joshua's completion of the land allotment, his reception of Timnath-serah, and his placement there of the stone knives from the wilderness circumcision (cf. Joshua 5:2–3; 19:49–50).
notes.22:8: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, in which Joshua speaks a parting exhortation to share the spoil, the Greek text narrates in the third person that the returning tribes departed with much wealth and divided the spoil with their brethren.
notes.22:10: The Greek text reads "Gilgal of the Jordan" here (and "Gilead of the Jordan" in verse 11) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Geliloth" (or the region of the Jordan).
notes.22:20: The Greek text preserves the name "Achar" (compare 1 Chronicles 2:7) instead of "Achan," and states "that one man alone died in his own sin" without the negation present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.22:29: "salamin" reflects the Greek text's transliteration of the Hebrew word shelamim ("peace offerings"), appearing here alongside the Greek equivalent "peace offering" (soterion).
notes.22:34: In the Greek text, Joshua himself names the altar of the eastern tribes and declares it a witness between them, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text attributes the naming to the sons of Reuben and Gad.
notes.23:4: The Greek clause is elliptical and reads "just as I spoke to you," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "I have allotted to you."
notes.23:5: The Greek text includes the promise that the Lord will send wild beasts against the remaining nations and their kings, a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:13: The Greek text renders the imagery as "nails in your heels and darts in your eyes," corresponding to "scourges on your sides and thorns in your eyes" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:16: The Greek text concludes the chapter here, without the final clause concerning the anger of the Lord burning against Israel found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.24:1: The Greek text places the covenant assembly at Shiloh (and again in v. 25, before the tabernacle of the God of Israel), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Shechem.
notes.24:5: Here the Greek shifts from the Lord's first-person speech (vv. 2-4) to Joshua narrating in the third person about the Lord and speaking of 'our fathers' (vv. 5-13), and omits the sending of Moses and Aaron found in the Hebrew.
notes.24:12: The Greek reads 'twelve kings of the Amorites,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'two kings of the Amorites.'
notes.24:31: The Greek places Joshua's burial north of 'Mount Gilead' (Hebrew: 'Mount Gaash') and adds the tradition that the stone knives used for the circumcision at Gilgal were laid in his tomb.
notes.24:33: The Greek concludes the book with an extended epilogue recounting Israel's carrying of the ark, the priesthood and burial of Phinehas, the worship of Astarte and Ashtaroth, and Israel's eighteen-year subjection to Eglon king of Moab (cf. Judges 3:12-14).
